Article Title: 'What is going on inside EC?' Union ministers, BJP allies call on poll body to clarify SIR row
Article Text:
Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the EC

What NDA allies said

Opposition raises allegations

NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Saturday called on the Election Commission EC to clarify amid the continuing row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Kumaraswamy said the responsibility for addressing reports of internal differences lay with the Election Commission itself and that the country needed to know what was actually happening within the constitutional body.“It is not the question of demands by any party or any leader. The responsibility of the Election Commission, that is important. What is the ground reality? What is going on inside the Election Commission?” Kumaraswamy said.His remarks came a day after three NDA allies Chirag Paswan's LJP(RV), Upendra Kushwaha's RLM and Chandrababu Naidu's TDP separately urged the Election Commission to address concerns surrounding the SIR exercise and reports of differences within the poll panel.Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the ECI.“The difference between what we are watching in the media and what is the real fact has to come out by these members. Because this is an important organisation, an autonomous body; why has it happened? That reality they must tell the media and the country. Their responsibility is greater. It is not an easy thing.Those three Election Commission members, including the chairman, what is the problem between them? What is the fault in that? Anything is there, they have to spell it,” he said.The issue gained traction after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period. The reports have prompted opposition demands for action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and calls to halt the SIR process.The ECI has maintained that differing views, internal notes and queries are part of its institutional functioning and said its final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.LJP(RV) chief and Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said he did not intend to “defend what is a constitutional body” but argued that the Election Commission should address public concerns directly.“If questions are being raised about its conduct, it is the responsibility of EC, especially the chief election commissioner (Gyanesh Kumar), to present its side firmly,” Paswan said.He added: “If people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy and, therefore, I think the EC must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying. But it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people.”RLM president Upendra Kushwaha also called for an immediate clarification, writing on social media, “There is considerable confusion among the public regarding the controversy surrounding SIR. This issue needs to be addressed. The EC should immediately clarify the situation to dispel this confusion.”The TDP too sought greater transparency. TDP parliamentary party neta Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu said, “The EC is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution.”Meanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Irfan Ansari criticised Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and alleged that names had been removed from electoral rolls.Speaking to ANI, Ansari alleged that the ECI had acted in a manner that benefited the BJP and questioned whether the poll panel would work according to the directions of a political party. The allegations were not independently established in his remarks.“I want to ask the citizens of the country, and I even want to ask the BJP voters: Names have been removed from the voter list; your name might have been removed too,” Ansari said.He also alleged that names of Muslims, Dalits and Adivasis had been deleted from voter lists and demanded that elections in Bihar be held again.“The Commission is an independent, neutral body. No political party should interfere with it,” he said, while alleging that Kumar had interfered and helped the BJP.
Article Summary: Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the ECI. The issue gained traction after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period.

Article Title: CCPA penalises Amazon, Flipkart, JioMart for selling unregistered herbicide
Article Text:
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product, Cyclosinone Herbicide.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds in lawns, gardens and agricultural fields.In separate orders issued recently, the consumer watchdog directed the e-commerce marketplaces to immediately discontinue the false and misleading advertisements and conduct a self-audit of their platforms to identify and remove products that violate the law or pose a risk to consumers’ life and safety.The CCPA initiated proceedings after the department of agriculture and farmers’ welfare forwarded a complaint it had received from the Crop Care Federation of India (CCFI) regarding the sale and advertisement of the unregistered herbicide through e-commerce and digital media platforms.During the investigation, the agriculture department informed CCPA that the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides and pesticides are regulated under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and the Insecticides Rules to safeguard human beings and animals from potential risks.The department told the authority that no chemical named Cyclosinone is included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act. However, a product marketed as “Cyclosinone Herbicide” was being sold through online platforms without disclosing the chemical name of its active ingredient or its composition.“It is currently being marketed illegally because it bypasses the mandatory safety, bio-efficacy, quality and legal checks required under the Insecticides Act,” the department said in its submission to CCPA.The authority rejected the e-commerce companies’ argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers. The CCPA said online marketplaces cannot disown their statutory obligation to protect consumers and are required to exercise due diligence to prevent the sale of products that are illegal or hazardous.
Article Summary: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart. Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former prime minister Manmohan Singh on his birth anniversary, remembering his long public life and service to the nation."Tributes to our former prime minister Dr Manmohan Singh Ji on his birth anniversary. He spent many years in public life and served the nation with dedication," PM Modi said in a post on X.Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi also paid floral tributes to the former prime minister on his birth anniversary.Sharing a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "On the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh ji, I pay my humble respects to him. With his humility, integrity, and foresight, he gave a new direction to the country's economy and social justice. His historic decisions and invaluable contributions to the making of India will forever continue to guide us."Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also paid tribute to Singh saying, "I offer my humble respects. As a skilled economist and successful politician, Dr Manmohan Singh ji imparted extraordinary momentum to India's development and elevated the nation's prosperity to new heights.""Through his visionary and inclusive economic policies, he enriched every section of society.Dr Manmohan Singh ji's unprecedented contributions to the country's development will always be remembered. I pay homage to his memories," he added.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also remembered the former prime minister, saying, "We remember with profound respect the extraordinary contribution of former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh to India’s nation-building. A visionary statesman, his landmark economic reforms transformed India’s growth trajectory, created new opportunities and helped lift millions out of poverty. His humility, integrity and wisdom defined his public life. ""He led with quiet dignity and compassion, placing inclusive growth and the welfare of the most vulnerable at the heart of governance. The rights-based framework of his government remains an enduring testament to this vision. On his birth anniversary, we pay our heartfelt homage to a statesman whose legacy of honest public service, inclusive development and transformative reforms will continue to inspire generations," he added.Manmohan Singh was born on September 26, 1932, in Gah, in present-day Pakistan, then part of undivided India. He died in New Delhi on December 26, 2024.Singh became India's 14th prime minister on May 22, 2004, and returned for a second consecutive term on May 22, 2009. He served as prime minister until 2014.Before becoming prime minister, Singh served as Union finance minister from 1991 to 1996. During his tenure, India introduced a wide-ranging programme of economic reforms that reshaped the country's economy and earned international recognition.Singh's public life spanned several decades, during which he held key positions in government and played a significant role in shaping India's economic policy.
Article Summary: Singh became India's 14th prime minister on May 22, 2004, and returned for a second consecutive term in 2009. He served as prime minister until 2014. During his tenure, India introduced a wide-ranging programme of economic reforms that reshaped the country's economy.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Saturday hit back at West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya after the latter said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar deserved the Padma Bhushan for his role in conducting the state’s recent assembly election and revising the voter list.Reacting to Bhattacharya’s remarks, Khera said, "The Padma Bhushan is a very small thing. Make him the Prime Minister. After all, a person who can make others Prime Minister should be made one himself."Bhattacharya had earlier praised the CEC while speaking to reporters at Panihati in North 24 Parganas district, saying the CEC deserved the Padma Bhushan "at the very least". He credited Kumar with ensuring a violence-free election in West Bengal and with "cleansing" the electoral roll by removing illegal Bangladeshi immigrants."Gyanesh Kumar deserves to be awarded, at the very least, with the Padma Bhushan. The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay, that there were no incidents of murder during the elections and people were actually allowed to cast their votes," the BJP leader said.He also claimed that Kumar had played a key role in the revision of the voter list."In a border state like West Bengal, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said."The people of West Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this. Therefore, the general public of West Bengal is grateful to Gyanesh Kumar and has blessed him with all their hearts," he added.The BJP leader’s comments came amid a growing controversy over the functioning of the Election Commission during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. An Indian Express report said that two election commissioners had objected to decisions allegedly taken in their names have triggered criticism from the Opposition.Also read: Unease within NDA over EC-SIR row? Three BJP allies seek poll body clarification as opposition keeps up pressure Congress has held nationwide protests demanding Kumar’s removal and arrest, while a plea has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging election-related orders and alleged software changes attributed to the CEC without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners.The row has also drawn criticism from Rahul Gandhi , who accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar of being "traitors" and alleged that they were destroying the foundation of India’s democracy by rigging elections.Bhattacharya, however, dismissed Gandhi’s remarks, saying, "The Congress itself doesn't pay heed to him. His own party doesn't take him seriously, and you are talking of Rahul Gandhi."

Article Title: 'No hard feelings': US on India's stern warning over Russia Sanctions Act
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The United States on Saturday said that it was looking to meet India's massive energy needs, days after US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas."We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs. We're increasing our hydrocarbon exports,” a senior US state department official told news agency PTI.“The demands are great, and the needs for oil are there. We are looking for alternatives. But I would say before even the war, India had been looking to diversify when it came to energy for a long time. It's not a new concept. We just need to expedite it faster,” he added.The US official also played down New Delhi's warning over the contentious law and said that India's response was expected after the US Congress took a pretty hard approach, especially publicly.“India has been looking for a long time to diversify its energy sources. They're a country that has massive energy needs,” the official told PTI.“You had members of Congress calling out India in particular, so of course India has to respond.We understand that. They have a domestic constituency, as do we. Like, there are no sort of hard feelings on any of that kind of activity," he added.Last week, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation’s potential impact on the US-India relationship.“This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side,” the ministry said.The official said that the new act gave President Trump a new tool in his toolbox.“That doesn't necessarily mean he deploys it tomorrow, but he has the opportunity to. His focus is on ending this war. It's been something he campaigned on and something he's been dedicated to from the beginning,” he said.“We're looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort. But I think you'll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine also the president, there's a scenario, the president uses that as well,” he added."Now, with President Trump's incredibly successful operation in Venezuela, we are moving into a better position that countries like India are going to be able to get access to that market,” he added.
Article Summary: U.S. looking to become a huge source of India's energy needs, says state department official. US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' last week. New Delhi warned the US of the legislation’s potential impact on the US-India relationship.

Article Title: NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi seeks more speaking time for SC/ST MPs in Parliament

NDA differences over SC/ST reservation

NEW DELHI: Union minister and NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, backing a BJP MP’s request for adequate speaking time for MPs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities during parliamentary discussions on important bills.In his letter, Manjhi said BJP MP Gajendra Singh Patel, who represents Khargone in Madhya Pradesh, had raised the issue during an “NDA MPs Group Dialogue Meeting” held at Manjhi’s Delhi residence on August 5.Patel had specifically requested that SC/ST MPs be given sufficient opportunity to raise issues concerning their communities on the floor of the House, Manjhi said.The Union minister has asked the Speaker to take further action on Patel’s request and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.Speaking to PTI, Patel confirmed that he had raised the issue and said the time allocated to SC/ST MPs should be increased further, as the speaking time allotted to each political party is divided among its MPs.“It is not that we do not get time, but we should get more time. More issues concerning SC/ST communities should be raised,” he said.Patel said the request was aimed at ensuring that issues concerning SC/ST communities receive adequate space during parliamentary discussions, while acknowledging that MPs from these communities do get opportunities to speak.Earlier last month, differences within the NDA came to the fore over the contentious issue of sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, with Manjhi and fellow Bihar-based Union minister Chirag Paswan taking divergent positions on the question of reviewing the reservation system.The debate intensified after HAM(S) president and Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman reiterated his party’s demand for sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, arguing that the most deprived communities should receive a greater share of the benefits.The Supreme Court’s August 1, 2024 Constitution Bench judgment allowing states to create sub-categories within SC and ST reservations has added a new dimension to the debate.Chirag strongly opposed any review of reservation and said Manjhi and his son should resign if they supported such measures.“The constitutional provision of SC/ST reservation is based on social discrimination and not economic status. If they want to change the Constitution, then debate the issue in Parliament. Those who talk or think about reviewing reservation should first resign, as they actually want to completely end it and reduce its scope,” Chirag said.He maintained that reservation was in place yesterday, is in place today and would continue in the future.Reacting to Chirag’s demand, Suman said he was ready to resign. “As far as resignations go, we are ready. My younger brother’s party is the bigger one; they have more numbers than us and are politically third-generation too — so let them take the lead. Let him step forward by resigning and we are prepared to resign alongside him,” he said.Suman maintained that reviewing reservation did not mean abolishing it. He said HAM(S) was seeking sub-categorisation, or a “quota within a quota”, so that communities at the bottom of the social and economic hierarchy could benefit.He cited Musahar, Bhuiyan, Dom, Halkhor and Nat communities as groups that continue to face deprivation and discrimination.JD(U) national general secretary and MLA Shyam Rajak, meanwhile, opposed any discussion on reviewing reservation and warned that tampering with the system could create serious social tensions. He said reservation was a constitutional right, not charity.The reservation debate has particular political significance in Bihar, where Dalit communities are socially diverse. The Nitish Kumar government introduced the Mahadalit category in 2007 to identify the most deprived Dalit communities.
Article Summary: Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. He has backed a BJP MP’s request for adequate speaking time for MPs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday clarified that the postponement of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's youth outreach events in Uttar Pradesh had nothing to do with the ongoing row over alleged internal differences in the poll body but were necessiated due to various logistical factors."Adjustments in dates of events is an ongoing process which is necessitated by various factors such as availability of venues, schedules of higher authorities, natural factors etc," officials said."There have been many occasions when the electoral literacy conferences had been postponed/dates changed earlier also such as HP, Ladakh, Uttarakhand. Moreover, the decision to postpone these two particular conferences was taken on Sep 21," they added.Gyanesh Kumar was scheduled to attend the voter awareness programmes in Meerut on Friday and Varanasi on September 28.This comes as a political row erupted after an Indian Express report highlighted differences among the commissioners over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The report said election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.Meanwhile, the opposition launched protests across the country demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The Madhya Pradesh Youth Congress held a protest outside the chief electoral officer’s office in Bhopal, demanding Kumar’s resignation. Protesters raised slogans against the CEC and carried posters reading “arrest Gyanesh Kumar for treason” and “Vote-Chori magic trick exposed”.In Dehradun, Congress workers also staged a protest demanding Kumar’s resignation, with Congress MP Kumari Selja leading the demonstration.In Punjab, Pradesh Congress committee president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring demanded Kumar’s dismissal, an FIR against him and his alleged collaborators, and their arrest. He also announced a march to the ECI office in Chandigarh under the leadership of Sachin Pilot.“The march will begin at 11 am on September 25 from near the RBI Office, Sector 17, Chandigarh, and proceed towards the ECI office,” he said.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also vowed to launch a nationwide protest from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday.In a post on X, Dipke said CJP would begin its protest from Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and subsequently take the agitation to cities across India.“If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by tomorrow, CJP will begin its nationwide protest from Mumbai on 2 October, and take it to cities across India. This Gandhi Jayanti let’s pledge to save democracy,” Dipke wrote.

Article Title: 'Dubai-based scammers looted Rs 94,000 crore': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE
Article Text:
Abhishek Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network

NEW DELHI:

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni. Kumar was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime.

NEW DELHI: Jantar Mantar in Delhi was heavily barricaded on Friday following nationwide protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Visuals from the protest site showed multiple layers of barricades, forming a clear cordon around Jantar Mantar. Buses have been used to block the entrances and there is heavy police deployment.The Indian Youth Congress was scheduled to march from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said on Friday that his organisation would launch nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday. A day earlier, he had warned of a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” agitation if the CEC refused to step down.Security personnel were also deployed outside the Election Commission office in New Delhi ahead of a Delhi Congress demonstration over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protests follow an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process.The report said their concerns included voter registration, deletion and restoration of names and access to electoral-roll databases.In Assam, state Congress president Gaurav Gogoi and several senior party leaders were detained while trying to cross police barricades during a protest demanding Kumar's removal, police said.Police also used water cannons to disperse protesters in Chandigarh and Patna.Gogoi had led a march from the Congress state headquarters, Rajiv Bhawan, towards the CEC's office, where the protesters planned to burn an effigy of the CEC. Article Summary: Congress-led protests against Kumar were held across several states. In Assam, state Congress president Gaurav Gogoi and several senior party leaders were detained, police said. NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from retrospective date of 2012. Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it. Article Title: 2027 UP assembly polls: Fight against BJP or Congress? Why Akhilesh’s ‘rath’ show in Raebareli is message for Rahul
Article Text:

INDIA bloc's failed Bihar experiment

Rahul or Akhilesh vs BJP

The Owaisi factor

Lok Sabha gains, assembly pains

NEW DELHI: Is Uttar Pradesh all set to go the Bihar way for the opposition’s INDIA bloc? Wait, we are not talking about the results yet. This is about the all-too-familiar alliance strains between INDIA bloc allies - the Samajwadi Party and the Congress in the run-up to UP assembly elections early next year.On Thursday, Akhilesh Yadav unveiled the Samajwadi Party's 'PDA Rath' which he will use for a statewide campaign in the run-up to the 2027 assembly poll. While his fight is against the BJP, the first stop of his rath was Raebareli - a Congress bastion represented by the Gandhis for decades.Also, while Akhilesh targeted the BJP, he had a clear message for the Congress also.“Alliance will happen. We will also go with the alliance. Winnability will be the criteria for deciding seats. For us, it is not about seats, it is about victory. Whosoever can win can take the seat.”The BJP was quick to take digs at both allies and suggested that now Congress should start its campaign from Yadav bastion Mainpuri.This was not an isolated remark. The SP and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar.Cut to the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.INDIA bloc allies - the RJD and the Congress engaged in a continuous war of words in Bihar over seat-sharing and CM face, while the BJP-led NDA managed a smooth division of seats. What started as public posturing between INDIA bloc allies ended up in public sparring between them as the divided opposition alliance was decimated in the polls.The two parties campaigned separately for most of the time as they could not agree on seat sharing. They took out separate yatras across the state. While Rahul Gandhi undertook the “Vote Adhikar Yatra,” RJD’s Tejashwi Yadav went across the state with his “Bihar Adhikar Yatra.” Ironically, it was the success of the two yatras that boomeranged on the alliance as it made seat-sharing bitter and difficult.In the run-up to the Bihar elections, Tejashwi Yadav was confident of a sweep. The Congress was also not willing to budge, guided by its improved showing in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state. The two parties used pressure tactics against each other. So much so that the INDIA bloc went into the elections as a divided house despite last-minute agreements and adjustments to keep the alliance intact.Uttar Pradesh appears to be headed the same way, at least as of now. We have already seen a lot of public posturing and sparring between the leaders of the INDIA bloc partners. Both the Congress and the SP have repeatedly claimed that the opposition’s fight against the BJP can be led only by their respective leaders.The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them, with the SP winning 37 and the Congress six. The alliance also won the Faizabad seat, which includes Ayodhya, where the BJP won in 2019.And that is perhaps where lies the genesis of this power tussle. Both the SP and the Congress feel that it was their party and leader who played a greater role in the 2024 electoral success and hence want the advantage to flow accordingly in seat sharing for the assembly elections.One look at the latest broadside between the two parties and we know why seat sharing between them may not be smooth.Recently, Samajwadi Party MP from Kairana Iqra Hasan and Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood, both elected in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as part of the SP-Congress alliance, publicly pitched their respective party leaders to take on the BJP."Only Rahul Gandhi is the opposition voice across the country, which unnerves the BJP. Rahul ji has done the hard work and created a favourable atmosphere. So make no mistake, nothing is possible without Rahul ji, and no one should have any doubts about this," Masood said.Days later, Hasan responded and pitched SP chief Yadav as the key to the alliance's prospects."Only Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. On its own, the Congress won't be able to achieve much," she said.Last week, Congress Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam signalled a firm stance regarding upcoming electoral negotiations and said that any seat-sharing arrangement with the Samajwadi Party (SP) must be built on mutual respect and equal standing.Clarifying reports regarding seat distribution, Gautam claimed that formal discussions with the SP have not yet begun. While expressing open flexibility for minor adjustments, he stressed that the Congress would not compromise its organisational self-respect or dignity in any prospective deal."We have made one thing very clear. The Congress is the country's oldest party. It was the Congress that led the freedom struggle. Any alliance formed will be based on mutual respect; there will be equal partnership and dignity. Sure, we can show some flexibility; there might be minor adjustments, but we cannot compromise on our dignity," the Congress leader said.The contrasting assertions come despite messages of unity from both sides of the divide. Akhilesh is riding high on SP’s Lok Sabha success in Uttar Pradesh. The Congress, which is trying hard to revive its lost electoral fortunes, does not want to compromise on its expansion plans in one of the most politically important states.The problem is that both the parties are wooing the same social base in the state - minorities, Dalits, women, youth. Akhilesh is missing no opportunity to expand his PDA’s - Pichda Dalit and Alpsankhyak - base by making concerted attempts to include Pandits, Aadhi aabadi (women) and other social groups. The Congress is also wooing the Brahmins, the Dalits and the women in a big way.What the two bickering allies don't realise that there are several other parties who are also reaching out to the same social base. For instance, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad are also going all out to woo Dalits. Then there is Owaisi, who has already put both the parties in a Catch22 situation by offering them an alliance against the BJP. Owaisi's proposal is like a double-edged sword for the two parties. If they accept his offer, the BJP will gun for them.If they reject the offer, Owaisi will use the rejection to rally the Muslims against them.The Samjawadi Party and the Congress may do well to learn lessons from the Bihar debacle before it’s too late. Lok Sabha elections and assembly elections are two very different games and success in one does not automatically translate into success in another. There are numerous instances to show that alliances which did well in Lok Sabha elections failed in assembly elections. Maharashtra is a case in point. The Maha Vikas Aghadi of the opposition parties - Congress, Shiv Sena and the NCP did very well in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, putting the BJP on the backfoot. But a year later in 2025 - the opposition alliance was decimated by the BJP in the assembly elections. So, Akhilesh and Rahul need to decide if they want to keep on flexing muscles at each other or unite in time to pose a challenge to the BJP.
Article Summary: The Samajwadi Party and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar. The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them.

Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%, lowering demand for a material that India largely imports to meet domestic requirements. They added that the modified bitumen could cost around 20% less than conventional bitumen.The waste plastic wet-process technology for producing premium-quality Waste Plastic Modified Bitumen (W-PMB 76-10) has been developed by IIT (BHU), Varanasi, under a research programme funded by the ministry of road transport and highways. The performance of the pilot stretch will be monitored by IIT (BHU) to assess its long-term engineering performance and field suitability, officials said.India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Until now, waste plastic has been used in road construction only as a dry mix with aggregates while laying the bituminous layer. The new method mixes processed waste plastic directly with bitumen before it is laid, making it the first such pilot on a national highway.Officials said the technology offers multiple benefits, including the value-added reuse of waste plastic through a scientifically controlled process and improved rut resistance of bituminous mixes under high ambient temperatures and heavy axle loads.The technology has also recently been granted a patent. The low-density polyethylene (LDPE) used in the process — a soft, flexible and lightweight thermoplastic made from petroleum — includes discarded irrigation pipes, waste files and plastic folders. The material has been processed with the support of local recyclers and MSMEs, creating an opportunity to integrate local waste recycling with infrastructure development.“Laboratory evaluations have shown that LDPE-modified bitumen provides better resistance to moisture damage and greater resistance to rutting at high temperatures. The modified binder increases the stiffness and high-temperature performance of asphalt, helping pavements withstand permanent deformation under heavy traffic loads and extreme temperatures,” an official said.
Article Summary: India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%.

Article Title: When food becomes a philosophy
Article Text:
“Pon karaya kaayum, mann karaya peyyum”

Pathitrupathu

Pulal Maruththal

“Kollaan Pulalai Maruththaanai Kaikooppi

Ella Uyirum Thozhum.”

ahimsa

Chandogya Upanishad

Purataasi arrives with the fragrance of devotion. The sixth month of the Tamil calendar, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is a month when many Tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food . Even confirmed meat lovers submit to this discipline. Some of my friends go berserk on the last day of Aavani, indulging in every imaginable meat delicacy!But Purataasi is more than a month of prayer. It is also a month of climatic transition. An old Tamil saying describes its extremes vividly:— the heat is so fierce that gold may melt, and the rain so heavy that the earth may erode. Perhaps, a gentler diet could give the digestive system some respite while the body adjusted to the changing weather.Vegetarianism itself must have emerged much later in the journey of humankind. Our earliest ancestors were certainly hunters and meat-eaters., in Sangam literature for instance, describes a preparation in which red meat was cooked with pulses and mixed with white rice — a dish that sounds remarkably like a distant ancestor of today's biryani.And yet, Thiruvalluvar gave vegetarianism an extraordinary ethical dimension. He devoted an entire chapter to— the refusal of meat. In Kural 260, he says:“One who does not kill and refuses to eat meat is worshipped by all living beings.”Valluvar did not present vegetarianism merely as a religious injunction. He seemed to locate it in something more elemental — compassion. His argument begins not with food, but with the refusal to cause harm.This has naturally led some scholars to see a possible Jain influence in Valluvar's thought. Jainism places, or non-violence, at the heart of spiritual life, and vegetarianism became one of its most rigorous expressions. The Jain understanding of food is deeply connected with the avoidance of harm and the accumulation of karma.The Jain tradition traces a powerful story of renunciation to Prince Neminatha, regarded as the 22nd Tirthankara. Neminatha was on his way to his wedding when he heard the cries of animals gathered to be slaughtered for the wedding feast. He turned away from the marriage, renounced his royal life and embraced the path of a Jain monk. The story transforms food into a moral question: what price should another life pay for our appetite?Interestingly, thespeaks of a teacher who instructed Krishna in asceticism and non-violence. Historian D D Kosambi suggested that this teacher may have been Neminatha himself, though this remains a historical conjecture.Today, vegetarianism has acquired another dimension. The growing popularity of veganism in the West is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare and the environmental footprint of livestock farming. Yet, paradoxically, in India — traditionally home to the world's largest vegetarian population — dietary habits are increasingly moving in the opposite direction.Perhaps the enduring wisdom of Valluvar lies not in telling us what must be on our plate, but in asking what lies within our heart. For him, refusing meat was not simply about food. It was about whether the mind could remain indifferent to the suffering of another living being.Sometimes, what we choose not to consume can reveal more about us than what we eat.
Article Summary: The sixth month of the Tamil calendar, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is a month when many Tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food. The growing popularity of veganism in the West is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare. Yet, paradoxically, in India, dietary habits are increasingly moving in the opposite direction.

Article Title: Lawyers move SC, AG for action on poll panel chief
Article Text:

As questions are being raised against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for allegedly unilaterally taking many decisions pertaining to the SIR drive, a Supreme Court lawyer has filed a petition in court seeking his criminal prosecution, and another has approached the attorney general, seeking his permission, as required under the law, to file a contempt petition against him.The petition filed in SC said action needed to be taken against the chief election commissioner for his "unilateral, unauthorised, and illegal decisions" taken in the name of EC. It referred to Section 18 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and the law laid down by a constitution bench in the TN Seshan case in 1995 to say EC's decisions mandatorily had to be taken by the majority.EC has maintained that all the decisions regarding special intensive revision of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by Kumar and his two colleagues, election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.The petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, echoing claims made in a news report, sought quashing of unauthorised modifications made to Form 6 on ECINet/ERONet portals requiring ancestry/last-SIR declarations, and also sought immediate restoration of the statutory Form 6 as prescribed under Registration of Electors Rules to permit all eligible adults to register as voters on the basis of original statutory requirements.Mentioning the alleged illegal acts of CEC, the petition said, "Introducing a mandatory ancestral condition (last SIR linkage) for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was explicitly branded as unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the commission."The petition said depriving decentralised electoral registration officers of their statutory authority under sections 13B, 22 and 23 of Representation of the People Act, 1950, and centralising electoral roll management under the director general of IT in Delhi was another wrong."Tampering with the electoral roll constitutes a cognisable offence under Section 32 of RP Act, 1950, as well as provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning falsification of records and public servants disobeying directions of law. In such a scenario, divested of any statutory or constitutional immunity, CEC remains directly accountable under the law - subject to police investigation, evidence gathering, and regular trial proceedings as an ordinary accused," the petition said, adding CEC could not claim immunity for illegal acts.It said CEC's act of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bore no "reasonable nexus" or legal connection to his official duties and fell squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constituted distinct, personal criminal liability.Another apex court advocate, Shiv Kumar Tripathi, wrote to the attorney general, bringing to his notice the "constitutional misconduct and contempt of court" by CEC and sought his approval to file a contempt case against him."SC has repeatedly emphasised EC's independence, impartiality and institutional integrity. CEC's office is one of constitutional primacy, but it is not intended to function as an authority overriding the equal constitutional status of other election commissioners in collective decision-making. Any departure from this constitutional framework may undermine public confidence in free and fair election," Tripathi said in his letter."I therefore respectfully request your good office to examine whether the reported conduct amounts to wilful disregard of binding judicial principles or directions of the Supreme Court, thereby attracting proceedings under Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, if legally sustainable," the letter said.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court lawyer has filed a petition in court seeking his criminal prosecution. Another has approached the attorney general, seeking his permission, as required under the law, to file a contempt petition against him. Article Summary: The matter came up for hearing before Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe. On Aug 18, SC had sought responses from Centre and state govts on the plea. The bench asked the respondents to file their counter affidavits and posted the matter after six weeks.

Article Title: SC notices to Tarun Tejpal, Goa police in 2013 rape case
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Friday issued two notices on Tarun Tejpal 's sentencing in a 2013 rape case - one to Goa Police on the journalist's petition against his 10-year prison term and the second to him on a Goa govt plea seeking enhancement of the sentence.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, submitted before an SC bench that it was a case where the acquittal was reversed by Bombay HC and urged that his bail plea be heard. Article Title: Blend social reforms with political work: PM Modi
Article Text:
PM tells cadre not to focus only on vote banks

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Friday asked BJP members to draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi to blend social reforms with their political work instead of focusing on vote bank politics."When we look at Mahatma Gandhi's life, we see he fought against the British and led the freedom movement. But he was also a great social reformer. He always worked against social evils. We as political workers too should not merely focus on vote-bank politics and allow things to continue as they are. We must continue working for social reforms," he said.He was interacting virtually with participants of "Seva Yatra", a motorcyle rally from Varanasi to Vadnagar organised by BJP to mark his 76th birthday and his continuous stint of 25 years as head of govt.Modi drew from his own experience as a frequent traveller across the length and breadth of India and said it has deeply enriched his life and values. "The message of service should be spread not merely by our words but action," he said, highlighting the felicitation of sanitation workers and other service-oriented programmes to make his point. Serving people is serving the country, he said, adding that BJP ideologue Deen Dayal Upadhyay, whose birth anniversary fell on Friday, put serving people at the core of his ideology.He praised those who carried out the cleanliness work in Prayagraj, noting that their efforts made the 'Kumbh Mela' famous worldwide for sanitation and elevated India's honour."So, I felt compelled to wash the feet of those who have enhanced India's honour so much, to seek their blessings," he said.Modi also said over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has significantly narrowed and infrastructure in villages has improved to a great extent. He said self-reliance among women has also increased in the country.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi asks BJP members to blend social reforms with their political work. He was interacting virtually with participants of "Seva Yatra" to mark his 76th birthday. Modi drew from his own experience as a frequent traveller across the length of India.

Article Title: Amazon, Flipkart & JioMart fined for illegal herbicide sale
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed for preventing and eliminating weeds.CCPA directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false advertisements and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety.Proceedings began after the department of agriculture and farmers' welfare forwarded a complaint from Crop Care Federation of India. The department said insecticides and pesticides are regulated under Insecticides Act, 1968, and Insecticides Rules. It said no chemical named Cyclosinone was listed in the Act's Schedule, and the product did not disclose its composition.CCPA rejected the companies' argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers.
Article Summary: CCPA directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false advertisements and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety. No chemical named Cyclosinone was listed in the Act's Schedule, and the product did not disclose its composition.

Article Title: PSU banks lift ATM charges in view of strike
Article Text:
PSBs, RRBs waive ATM fees ahead of 3-day strike

NEW DELHI: Public sector banks and regional rural banks have announced their decision to waive ATM charges to ensure hassle-free cash withdrawal by their customers from Sept 28-30 due to the strike called by employee unions.Besides, all branches of state-run banks and RRB will remain open on Sunday as the unions have called a three-day strike starting Monday. "Withdrawals from other bank ATMs can be made without charges from 26th to 30th Sept," Indian Bank said. HDFC said its branches will remain open Sunday and it will be business as usual during the strike.Govt earlier asked for payment of salaries and pension to retired personnel ahead of time to avoid the impact of strike. Article Summary: State-run banks and RRB will remain open on Sunday as the unions have called a three-day strike starting Monday. "Withdrawals from other bank ATMs can be made without charges from 26th to 30th Sept," Indian Bank said. Govt earlier asked for payment of salaries and pension to retired personnel ahead of time.
